sentences.text: The name Dactylosaurus translates to "finger lizard" or "finger reptile" from Greek, describing a small reptile that grew to a maximum length of 50 cm.
Its skeleton included 17 cervical vertebrae with cervical ribs featuring anterior processes.
The genus Dactylosaurus was first described by Gürich in 1884.
The single forelimb found on the holotype had a slimmer radius and ulna compared to the similar European nothosaur Neusticosaurus.
Dactylosaurus is classified under the class Reptilia as a genus of nothosaur within the family Pachypleurosauridae.
The species Dactylosaurus gracilis is the smallest known species within its family, Pachypleurosauridae.
Dactylosaurus lived in central Europe during the Early and Middle Triassic periods, specifically the Late Olenekian and Anisian stages.
A new site in Gogolin containing abundant remains of Dactylosaurus was discovered in 2012 and dates to approximately 247 million years ago.
